actix.description: Actix-web 4 with rustls for TLS. Standard configuration: actix-files serves static content from disk per request via try_compressed(), which selects a pre-compressed .br/.gz sibling by Accept-Encoding through the framework API (no hand-rolled suffix lookup); the Compress middleware compresses dynamic responses (json-comp) on-the-fly. deadpool-postgres for async DB pooling (sized from DATABASE_MAX_CONN); crud reads go through an in-memory cache-aside (X-Cache MISS/HIT, invalidated on update — no Redis required). json-tls is served over HTTP/1.1-with-TLS on :8081; baseline-h2/static-h2 over h2 on :8443. serde_json per request. Pinned to actix git main for try_compressed() (unreleased in actix-files 0.6.10). Compiled with -O3 and thin LTO.

variants.description: Actix-web 4 h2c-only listener on port 8082 using bind_auto_h2c. A middleware rejects HTTP/1.1 requests so the port serves HTTP/2 cleartext prior-knowledge exclusively. Handlers share the same shape as the main actix entry (serde_json per request).
Actix-web WebSocket echo server

aiohttp.description: aiohttp 3.14 web server on uvloop, one forked worker per core sharing the port with SO_REUSEPORT. Routing through the aiohttp router, JSON through web.json_response, gzip through the built-in response compression.

araara-standard.description: araara - an OCaml 5 web stack built on HCS, using HCS server defaults where possible for the HttpArena harness. Eio, radix-trie routing, Phoenix-style plugs, Postgres via repodb, gzip/zstd compression. HTTP/3 and gRPC are not implemented.

araara.description: araara - an OCaml 5 web stack built on HCS, Eio, a zero-copy sans-I/O HTTP codec, radix-trie routing, Phoenix-style plugs, Postgres via repodb, and gzip/zstd compression. HTTP/3 and gRPC are not implemented.

aspnet-minimal.description: Minimal ASP.NET Core server using .NET 10 with Kestrel and minimal API routing.

variants.description: ASP.NET Core gRPC server using .NET 10 preview with Kestrel.
ASP.NET Core WebSocket echo server using .NET 10 preview with Kestrel and minimal API.

aspnet-minimal-ioxide.description: Minimal ASP.NET Core (.NET 11) on the ioxide io_uring transport (ioxide.Kestrel via UseIoxide(), default reactor count). Same app as aspnet-minimal — only the Kestrel transport differs. HTTP/1.1 only: plaintext plus HTTP/1.1-over-TLS (json-tls) terminated in the transport via kTLS (ioxide.tls). HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 are not enabled.

aspnet-minimal + caddy.description: ASP.NET minimal API behind Caddy, serving HTTP/3 (QUIC) at the edge with h1 forwarding to Kestrel.

aspnet-minimal + nginx.description: ASP.NET Core minimal API behind an Nginx reverse proxy. Nginx handles TLS termination and static files, proxying dynamic endpoints to Kestrel over HTTP/1.1.

axum.description: Axum 0.8 on hyper with the multi-threaded Tokio runtime, default configuration. Routing and path/query extractors through the Axum API, serde_json via the Json response, gzip through the tower-http compression layer.

bananabread.description: Seagreen — a TypeScript port of GenHTTP — on Bun's raw-TCP engine, with kotlinx-style decorators and Bun's built-in SQL.

beskar-websocket.description: High-performance WebSocket echo server built with Beskar.Networking.

bjoern.description: A screamingly fast, ultra-lightweight WSGI server

blackbull.description: BlackBull — pure-Python async ASGI 3.0 framework supporting HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, and WebSocket. ALPN negotiates HTTP/2 on the same listener that serves HTTP/1.1.

bottle.description: Fast, simple and lightweight WSGI micro web-framework for Python

bun.description: Bun.serve, Bun's own HTTP server, with no framework on top and one process per core sharing the port.

caddy.description: Caddy with custom Go handler modules compiled in via xcaddy: httparena for /baseline11 and /baseline2, httparena_json for /json/{count}, serializing the JSON body per request from the dataset read at provision time. Native file_server for /static. HTTP/1.1 on :8080, h1 over TLS on :8081, h2 and h3 on :8443.

cadente.description: Cadente is a standalone managed HTTP/1.1 server for .NET, running directly on sockets without the Sisk framework layer.

cardigan.description: Java HTTP engine built on io_uring, Panama FFI, virtual threads, and thread-per-core event loops.

variants.description: Cardigan gRPC over cleartext HTTP/2 prior knowledge.
Cardigan gRPC over HTTP/2 and TLS.
Cardigan HTTP/2 over TLS.
Cardigan HTTP/2 over cleartext prior knowledge.
Cardigan HTTP/1.1 over TLS.

carter.description: Carter 10 on ASP.NET Core and Kestrel, default configuration. Routes declared in a Carter module and mapped onto the endpoint router, JSON through System.Text.Json, gzip and brotli through ResponseCompression at level 1, json-tls on 8081.

chi.description: chi v5 router on the Go net/http server, default configuration. Routing and path parameters through the chi API, encoding/json for the response body, gzip through the chi middleware.Compress middleware.

dart-io.description: Stock Dart HttpServer baseline in the same SDK lineage as dart-zig, with optional JIT/AOT runtime mode via DART_IO_MODE for direct PR comparisons.

dart-zig.description: dart-zig custom Dart runtime on Linux io_uring, using the reusable dart-zig runtime and builder images, with the benchmark app source owned by HttpArena. Current integration targets baseline, pipelined, limited-conn, and json.

deno.description: Deno's own HTTP server, Deno.serve, with no framework and no router on top. The only dependencies are pg and ioredis over npm: specifiers, which the database profiles cannot run without.

django.description: Django 6.1 as an ASGI application on Uvicorn. URLconf routing and path converters through the Django API, JsonResponse for the JSON payload, GZipMiddleware for compression.

drogon.description: Drogon on the trantor event loop, one event loop per core. Routing and path/query params through the Drogon API, jsoncpp serialization, gzip through the built-in response compression.

echo.description: Echo v4 on the Go net/http server, default configuration. Routing and path/query binding through the Echo API, encoding/json via c.JSON, gzip through the Echo Gzip middleware.

effinitive.description: Ultra-high-performance custom HTTP server for .NET 10 — built from scratch for maximum speed.

express.description: Express 5 on node:http with the cluster module for multi-core scaling.

fastapi.description: FastAPI async web framework on Uvicorn (uvloop)

fastendpoints.description: FastEndpoints (REPR-pattern endpoint framework on ASP.NET Core) using .NET 10 with Kestrel.

fasthttp.description: fasthttp is a raw multi-threaded epoll HTTP server in V's standard library (non-blocking, SO_REUSEPORT, one worker per core). It uses fasthttp's zero-copy append handler (write the raw response straight into the connection's reused buffer), lock-free per-worker state (make_state), deterministic request framing that reassembles TCP-fragmented AND chunked requests (so baseline is now subscribed), and sendfile(2) for static bodies. JSON is built in a single allocation with precomputed prefixes (no per-request reflection); json-comp gzips on Accept-Encoding with a process-shared cache; static assets are streamed via sendfile with a preloaded MIME/size table; crud is an in-memory cache-aside (X-Cache MISS/HIT, invalidated on update); fortunes renders the DB rows + a runtime row with HTML escaping; async-db/crud/fortunes use the stdlib db.pg pooled Go-style DB (blocking queries on the worker thread — fasthttp has no async watch reactor yet). Built on pinned V master 84a76d791 (the fasthttp vanilla-architecture refactor, vlang/v#27771) with the default GC (Boehm). json-tls is not subscribed: the stdlib fasthttp server has no TLS backend.

fastify.description: Fastify 5 on node:http with the cluster module for multi-core scaling.

fastpysgi-asgi.description: An ultra fast WSGI/ASGI server for Python

fastpysgi-wsgi.description: An ultra fast WSGI/ASGI server for Python

fiber-tuned.description: Fiber 3 on fasthttp, the fiber entry with what it leaves at default: sonic behind c.JSON, the compress middleware at best speed (brotli 0, gzip 1), the Postgres pool filled at startup, and fasthttp at master for its go-brrr brotli. Same routes, prefork, static and TLS paths as fiber.

fiber.description: Fiber 3 on fasthttp, default configuration, one prefork child per logical CPU sharing the port. Routing and typed path/query binding through the Fiber API, JSON via c.JSON, gzip and brotli through the compress middleware, static files from the pre-compressed .br/.gz siblings on disk.

flask.description: Flask web framework on Gunicorn with sync workers

fletch.description: Express-inspired HTTP framework for Dart with radix-tree routing, middleware chains, signed sessions, and built-in DI.

frankenphp-trueasync.description: FrankenPHP with TrueAsync coroutine engine. Each HTTP request runs as a cooperative coroutine with PDO connection pooling, async I/O, and OPcache JIT. Built on Caddy with native HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 support.

fulmine-tuned.description: fulmine.js with the caches its standard entry has to leave off: the in-memory small-file cache and the stat cache, both shipped settings, both forbidden to a standard entry because they keep a static request off the disk.

fulmine.description: fulmine.js (drop-in Express 5 on uWebSockets.js) with its own cluster option for multi-core scaling.

genhttp-ioxide.description: GenHTTP 11 on .NET 11 on a custom io_uring server engine (the ioxide runtime) instead of the default socket engine. Uses GenHTTP's published ioxide engine packages (GenHTTP.Engine.Ioxide / GenHTTP.Modules.IoxideFiles, PR #860, merged). Responses go through GenHTTP's own routing + serialization; Postgres rides ioxide.pg (per-reactor ring-native pool) and json-tls rides ioxide.tls (kTLS TX) on :8081.

genhttp-kestrel.description: Lightweight, embeddable and modular C# web server.

genhttp.description: Lightweight, embeddable and modular C# web server.

gin.description: Gin web framework on the Go net/http server, default configuration. Routing and path/query binding through the Gin API, encoding/json via c.JSON, gzip through the gin-contrib/gzip middleware.

go-fasthttp.description: High-performance Go HTTP server using fasthttp with zero-allocation design and buffer reuse.

go-stdlib.description: The Go standard library net/http server with no framework, default configuration. Routing through the ServeMux method and wildcard patterns of Go 1.22, JSON through encoding/json, gzip written by hand with compress/gzip because the standard library ships no compression middleware.

go-websocket.description: Go WebSocket echo server using gobwas/ws

h2o-mruby.description: h2o config-based server with mruby handlers and native HTTP/3 (QUIC) support.

h2o.description: High-performance C HTTP server using libh2o with multi-threaded event loops and native HTTP/2 support. Handlers answer /baseline11, /baseline2, /json/{count} — serialized per request from the dataset parsed at startup — and /static from files preloaded at boot. TLS on :8081 (HTTP/1.1) and :8443 (h2). No HTTP/3: libh2o's QUIC stack is not wired up in this embedded server.

hanami.description: Hanami 2.3 actions and router on Puma, one worker per core. Routing and params through the Hanami API, JSON generated per request, gzip through Rack::Deflater.

helidon-production.description: Helidon SE 4.5.4 on Níma WebServer with Java 25, config-based static content, HTTP/2, gRPC, and WebSocket support.

helidon-tuned.description: Helidon SE 4.5.4 on Níma WebServer with Java 25, tuned socket and protocol-validation settings, precompressed static content, HTTP/2, gRPC, and WebSocket support.

hical.description: Hical is a modern C++20/26 high-performance web framework built on Boost.Asio, featuring coroutine-based async I/O (boost::asio::awaitable<T>), three-tier PMR memory pools, zero-copy HTTP parsing via picohttpparser, and a self-developed WebSocket stack (RFC 6455 with permessage-deflate). SO_REUSEPORT multi-acceptor model on Linux. Dual-track C++26 reflection layer (P2996 / C++20 macro fallback).

hono-bun.description: Ultrafast Web Standards framework running natively on Bun — no adapter overhead.

hono-node.description: Hono on node:http through @hono/node-server, with the cluster module for multi-core scaling.

http-kit.description: Ring-compatible benchmark entry using blocking JDBC on http-kit's virtual request workers.

http4k.description: http4k 6 on the Undertow backend, default configuration. Routing and path/query access through the http4k API, Jackson JSON, gzip through the http4k GZip server filter.

http4s.description: http4s 0.23 on the Ember server with cats-effect, default configuration. Routing through the http4s DSL, circe JSON, gzip through the http4s GZip middleware.

http.jl.description: HTTP.jl 2 on its Reseau transport, one process with one interactive thread per core. Routing on the stream handler, JSON through JSON3, gzip by hand with CodecZlib because HTTP.jl ships no compression middleware. json-tls on 8081 through Reseau's TLS listener, the transport HTTP.jl already ships.

humming-bird.description: Lightweight, flexible HTTP server framework written in Swift, built on SwiftNIO with minimal dependencies.

hyper-express.description: hyper-express (Express-like API on uWebSockets.js) with the cluster module for multi-core scaling.

hyper.description: Low-level HTTP library for Rust, built on tokio with multi-threaded async runtime.

hyperf.description: A coroutine framework that focuses on hyperspeed and flexibility. Building microservice or middleware with ease.

ioxide.description: ioxide — a shared-nothing io_uring runtime for .NET, consumed as its published NuGet packages (ioxide, ioxide.pg, ioxide.timer, ioxide.file, ioxide.http2, ioxide.ngtcp2, ioxide.nghttp3). One ring per reactor thread: multishot accept/recv into provided buffer rings, inline IValueTaskSource continuations, raw-syscall io_uring (no liburing). The HTTP/1.1 handler (request line, headers, Content-Length + chunked bodies, keep-alive, pipelining, fragmented reads) is hand-written on the raw recv/send API; TLS terminates ring-natively (kTLS transmit offload, OpenSSL receive) on :8081, h2 over TLS (pure-C# ioxide.http2) on :8443, and HTTP/3 over QUIC (ngtcp2 + nghttp3) on udp:8443; async-db rides ioxide.pg's ring-native pooled Postgres driver (SCRAM-SHA-256), static on h1 reads the file descriptor straight into the connection's write slab (ioxide.file hands out descriptors, not bytes), so header and body leave in one flush with no intermediate buffer; h2/h3 serve the same assets from memory.

iris.description: Thread-per-core C++ HTTP/1.1 gateway on epoll/SO_REUSEPORT with a hand-written incremental parser. Zero-allocation steady state: fixed per-connection buffers, precomputed response templates, per-request JSON serialization from the mounted dataset, static assets served via precompressed .br/.gz negotiation with Linux sendfile from sealed memfd responses, streaming POST /upload body counting, OpenSSL TLS on :8081 for json-tls, and async libpq for async-db.

jooby.description: Jooby 3.9 on Jetty in the script API. Routing and path/query values through Jooby's Context, JSON through the Jackson module, gzip through the built-in compression at level 1, json-tls on 8081.

koa.description: Koa 3 on the Node http server, default configuration, one cluster worker per core. Routing through @koa/router, JSON through the koa response body, gzip through koa-compress.

ktor-ghost.description: JetBrains Ktor 3.x on Netty with Kotlin coroutines, Ghost Serializer, JDK 21.

ktor.description: JetBrains Ktor 3.x on Netty with Kotlin coroutines, kotlinx.serialization, JDK 21.

lapis.description: Lapis on OpenResty with LuaJIT, one nginx worker per core. Routing and params through the Lapis application API, cjson serialization, gzip through the nginx gzip directive.

laravel.description: Laravel 13 served by Laravel Octane on FrankenPHP, the first-party production runtime documented by Laravel. Routing and request handling through the Laravel API, responses via the response()/json() helpers, gzip and brotli through the Caddy encode directive Octane generates.

libreactorng.description: libreactorng — Fredrik Widlund's io_uring-native event framework, the successor to the long-running epoll-based libreactor. Built directly on Linux io_uring syscalls with zero third-party runtime deps. Minimal server dispatches /pipeline, /baseline11, /baseline2 via the built-in HTTP parser; one reactor process per logical CPU via SO_REUSEPORT.

litestar.description: Litestar 2 on uvicorn with uvloop and httptools, one worker per core. Routing and parameter injection through the Litestar API, msgspec JSON serialization, gzip through the Litestar compression config.

lithium.description: Lithium's header-only HTTP server on its epoll/fiber backend. Disabled: lithium's own JSON serializer writes booleans as 1/0 rather than true/false, which the json profile rejects, and its decoder cannot read a JSON boolean at all.

may-minihttp.description: Mini HTTP server built on May stackful coroutines. Uses cooperative scheduling with coroutine-per-connection model for high concurrency.

micronaut.description: Micronaut 5 on the Netty HTTP server, default configuration, running on the JVM and not on native-image. Routing and injection are generated at compile time by the Micronaut annotation processor, JSON through Jackson, gzip through the Netty server compression the framework enables by itself.

minima-sync.description: A synchronous single-issuer io_uring HTTP/1.1 server on Minima's io_uring bindings, NativeAOT-compiled. One pinned reactor thread per core (SO_REUSEPORT, SINGLE_ISSUER|DEFER_TASKRUN); multishot accept + single-shot recv into per-connection buffers (parse-in-place); responses serialized straight into the send buffer; recv/send alternate fully inline — no async, no thread pool, no GC on the hot path. JSON serialized per request from the model.

minima-ws.description: Hand-rolled WebSocket echo on the Minima engine — a from-scratch C# multi-reactor io_uring server (direct io_uring syscalls via libc, multishot accept + multishot recv into a provided buffer ring, one ring per core with SO_REUSEPORT). The RFC 6455 handshake and the frame parser/masking/echo are written by hand on Minima's raw recv/send API; no WebSocket library.

minima.description: Minima — a from-scratch C# multi-reactor io_uring HTTP/1.1 server. Per-reactor SO_REUSEPORT + multishot accept, multishot recv into a provided buffer ring, inline (RCA=false) continuations with a reactor-thread short-circuit on buffer return/flush/recycle. The engine is vendored unchanged; the request handler (request line, headers, Content-Length + chunked bodies, keep-alive, pipelining, fragmented reads) is hand-written on its raw recv/send API. No HTTP framework.

mojolicious.description: Mojolicious 9 on Mojo::Server::Prefork, the server hypnotoad runs, one worker per core. Routing through Mojolicious::Lite, JSON through Mojo::JSON, gzip through the renderer's own compression.

mq-bridge-py.description: mq-bridge Python bindings (mq_bridge_py). A single http->response route dispatches on request metadata while HTTP framing stays in Rust; cleartext HTTP/1.1 + h2c run on 8080/8082, optional TLS listeners serve HTTP/2 on 8443 and HTTP/1.1 on 8081, and the inline-response fast path keeps responses off the GIL so the Python handler runs only the per-request dispatch. Postgres via psycopg for async-db, crud (Redis cache-aside) and fortunes, which renders per request with the Jinja2 template engine; static assets are read from /data/static per request, serving the on-disk .gz variant when the client accepts it; /delay waits with a blocking sleep, so async concurrency is the worker-process count.

mq-bridge.description: mq-bridge async message-bridging library run as an HTTP server. A single catch-all http->response route dispatches on request metadata and replies through mq-bridge's inline-response fast path; hyper-util's auto connection builder serves HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 prior-knowledge (h2c) on the cleartext port (8080) and HTTP/2-over-TLS (ALPN h2) on 8443. Postgres via the library's re-exported sqlx for async-db and crud (in-process cache-aside, one-second TTL), fortunes rendered per request with the Askama template engine, dataset read from /data/dataset.json, static assets from /data/static, response compression negotiated per request by the library from Accept-Encoding (zstd > gzip > lz4).

variants.description: mq-bridge WebSocket echo server. A websocket->response route echoes each inbound text/binary frame back on the same connection via the direct WebSocket response path.

nestjs.description: NestJS 11 on the Express platform adapter, default configuration. Routing and parameter decorators through the Nest API, controller return values serialized by the framework, gzip through the compression middleware the Nest docs recommend.

nginx.description: Nginx with a custom C handler module, compiled with -O3 -march=native. The module answers /baseline11, /baseline2 and /json/{count}, serializing the JSON body per request from the dataset parsed at worker startup; /static/* is served by nginx core's sendfile path. TLS via quictls: HTTP/1.1 on :8081, h2 and h3 on :8443.

ngx-php.description: Embedded PHP scripting language module for nginx.

node-h3.description: H3 v2, the unjs framework under Nitro and Nuxt, served on node:http by srvx with the cluster module for multi-core scaling.

node-websocket.description: Node.js WebSocket echo server using ws package

node.description: Node's own HTTP server, node:http, with no framework and no router, and one worker per core sharing the port through reusePort. The only dependencies are pg and ioredis, which the database profiles cannot run without.

ntex.description: ntex 2 on its own tokio-backed runtime, default configuration. Routing and extractors through ntex::web, JSON through serde_json, gzip negotiated in the handler at level 1, json-tls on 8081 through rustls.

oxpecker.description: F# web framework built on ASP.NET Core endpoint routing, with a functional handler DSL and its own code-as-markup view engine.

pedestal.description: Pedestal connector-map benchmark entry using the standard Jetty-backed server.

phoenix-bandit.description: High-performance Elixir framework using Phoenix and Bandit HTTP server, leveraging Erlang/OTP for concurrent networking and asynchronous database operations.

pico.description: A raw V server on the picoev non-blocking event loop + picohttpparser (both stdlib). One process per core shares the listen socket via SO_REUSEPORT. JSON is serialized manually (precomputed prefixes, no per-request reflection). Built with the default GC on pinned V master c0624b274. DB profiles are not subscribed: picoev is a single-threaded event loop and the stdlib db.pg driver is blocking, which would stall the loop. baseline is not subscribed: picoev parses each recv() in one shot and does not reassemble TCP-fragmented requests, which baseline validation requires.

plug-cowboy.description: Plug on the Cowboy adapter without Phoenix. Routing through Plug.Router, Jason JSON encoding, gzip through the cowboy_compress_h stream handler.

pyronova.description: Pyronova — Python web framework with a Rust core (hyper + tokio + rustls + mimalloc) and PEP 684 sub-interpreter workers for true multi-core parallelism. Opt-in features: gzip/brotli compression, rustls TLS with h2/h1 ALPN, streaming body ingest, async Postgres via sqlx::PgPool. Handlers are standard Python functions routed via decorators.

quarkus-jvm.description: Quarkus with RESTEasy Reactive on Vert.x/Netty, JDK 21, optimized JVM tuning.

variants.description: Quarkus gRPC server using quarkus-grpc on Vert.x with h2c, JDK 21, optimized JVM tuning.

Standalone Vert.x 4.5 on JDK 25, shaded fat jar. One Vertx instance per CPU so each HttpServer binds its own listening socket with SO_REUSEPORT (Netty epoll native transport) — the kernel distributes accepts across cores. Quarkus proper is not used here: its package step filters classifier-carrying jars like netty-transport-native-epoll out of the runtime image, and without native transport SO_REUSEPORT is a no-op. The HTTP stack (Vert.x + Netty epoll) is identical to what quarkus-jvm uses underneath. HTTP/1.1 is rejected by the handler with 400 to keep the port h2c-only.

rack-falcon.description: A high-performance web server for Ruby

rack-iodine.description: Iodine is a fast concurrent web application for Ruby

rage.description: Rage is a modern Ruby framework designed for non-blocking I/O and simpler infrastructure

rails.description: Ruby on Rails (API mode) on Puma, multi-worker with one worker per CPU core.

reitit.description: Reitit 0.9 routing on Ring and the Jetty adapter, default configuration. Routes and path parameters through reitit.ring, query parsing through ring's wrap-params on the router, JSON through clojure.data.json, gzip through Jetty's GzipHandler, json-tls on 8081.

ring-jetty-adapter.description: Ring application using the official Ring Jetty adapter and standard Ring middleware.

ring-jetty9-adapter.description: Ring application using the Sunng ring-jetty9-adapter on modern Jetty.

ringzero-ws.description: Hand-rolled WebSocket echo server on raw io_uring (liburing) — no WebSocket library. Multishot accept + multishot recv into a provided buffer ring for zero-copy ingest, one ring per core with SO_REUSEPORT, and a from-scratch RFC 6455 handshake (hand-written SHA-1 + base64) and frame parser/masking.

ringzero.description: Custom C HTTP server built on io_uring with a multi-reactor architecture. No epoll, no thread-per-connection.

roadrunner.description: Roadrunner: pure-Erlang HTTP/1.1 + HTTP/2 + HTTP/3 + WebSocket server from the Arizona framework.

robyn.description: Robyn is a High-Performance Web Framework with a Rust runtime

rocket.description: Rocket 0.5 on hyper with the multi-threaded Tokio runtime, default configuration. Routing, path and query guards through the Rocket API, serde_json via the Json responder.

rust-epoll.description: Zero-dependency Rust HTTP engine using raw epoll syscalls, one-thread-per-core with SO_REUSEPORT.

salvo.description: Salvo 0.96 on tokio and hyper, default configuration. Routing through the Router tree, JSON through salvo's Json responder, gzip and brotli through the built-in Compression hoop at level 1, json-tls on 8081 through rustls.

sanic.description: Sanic 25.3 on its own server with uvloop and httptools, one worker per core through the Sanic worker manager. Routing through the Sanic router, JSON through the ujson response, streamed uploads. Sanic ships no compression middleware, so gzip is hand-rolled in a response middleware, hence tuned.

sark.description: sark — Rust HTTP on the dope io_uring runtime: thread-per-core, zero-copy parsing, type-safe routing, cartel-pg for Postgres. No serde, no tokio, no Arc/atomic.

variants.description: sark behind a stock Caddy edge (TLS + h2/h3) — gateway profiles. Caddy terminates TLS and serves static from disk; sark serves dynamic endpoints over TCP. No tokio, no Arc/atomic.
sark HTTP/3 over QUIC on the dope io_uring runtime: native QUIC endpoint as a dope Manifold, shin TLS 1.3 with self-signed Ed25519 X.509 cert, QPACK. Thread-per-core, no tokio, no Arc/atomic.
sark production stack — nginx edge (TLS + JWT auth_request) + redis cache + shared authsvc in front of the sark io_uring server. Cache-aside, stateless JWT. No tokio, no Arc/atomic.

servicestack.description: One framework to power them all. Write your HTTP APIs once and take advantage of end to end typed integrations for all popular Web, Mobile and Desktop platforms.

simplew-tuned.description: SimpleW is Modern Web Server for .NET. Designed for Simplicity. Built for Speed.

simplew.description: SimpleW is Modern Web Server for .NET. Designed for Simplicity. Built for Speed.

sinatra.description: Sinatra DSL web framework on Puma, multi-threaded with one worker per CPU core.

sisk.description: Sisk is a lightweight, agnostic, simple, and robust web development framework.

slim.description: Slim 4 with slim/psr7 on FrankenPHP in classic per-request mode. Routing and PSR-7 request/response through the Slim API, json_encode per request, gzip through the FrankenPHP encode directive.

slimeweb.description: SlimeWeb is a fast lightweight framework for python powered by rust

socketify.description: socketify.py 0.0.31 on its uWebSockets bindings, one process per core per port sharing the port through SO_REUSEPORT. Disabled: socketify's bundled libsocketify rejects a request whose request line is split across TCP segments, which fails the fragmentation suite. The uWebSockets.js entries here are unaffected.

spring-boot.description: Spring Boot with embedded Tomcat on JDK 25 with virtual threads.

spring-jvm-grpc.description: Spring Boot gRPC server using grpc-spring-boot-starter with Netty transport on JDK 24.

starlette.description: Starlette 1.6 on uvicorn (uvloop), one worker per core, same uvicorn configuration as the fastapi entry. Routing through Starlette routes, JSON through JSONResponse, gzip through the Starlette GZipMiddleware.

swerver.description: Experimental Zig web framework built directly on swerver's Router, HandlerContext, middleware, response, and static-file APIs. No pre-computed response bodies (pre-encoded registry off); JSON is serialized per request through ctx.jsonValue; unary gRPC is decoded and encoded per request over h2c and TLS h2; async-db and fortunes use the native async PostgreSQL client (pipelining, prepared-statement cache, park/resume). Single-threaded event loop per worker, SO_REUSEPORT fork fan-out, one multi-listener process for HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, HTTP/3 (QUIC), kqueue, epoll, and io_uring backends.

swoole.description: Swoole is an event-driven, asynchronous, coroutine-based concurrency library with high performance for PHP.

variants.description: Swoole is an event-driven, asynchronous, coroutine-based concurrency library with high performance for PHP.

trillium-tuned.description: Trillium 1.x with one current_thread tokio runtime per CPU, SO_REUSEPORT TCP sharding (single QUIC endpoint for h3), tuned HttpConfig (larger response/body buffers, 64K h2 frames, eager body preallocation), and static files preloaded into memory at startup. sonic-rs for JSON, deadpool-postgres, mimalloc, trillium-grpc for the benchmark.BenchmarkService gRPC endpoints.

trillium.description: Trillium 1.x async Rust web framework on tokio. trillium-rustls for TLS (h1 + h2 via ALPN), trillium-quinn for HTTP/3, trillium-websockets for /ws, trillium-static for /static/* served from disk per request, trillium-compression middleware for runtime gzip/brotli, trillium-api for JSON handlers, trillium-grpc for the benchmark.BenchmarkService gRPC endpoints, deadpool-postgres for async-db and crud.

true-async-server.description: Native PHP HTTP server built on the TrueAsync coroutine engine. Each connection runs as a cooperative coroutine; one OS thread per CPU listens via SO_REUSEPORT inside a single PHP process. PDO connection pool, OPcache JIT, no Caddy / FrankenPHP / FastCGI in front.

vanilla-epoll.description: vanilla is a minimalist, high-performance HTTP server written in V: multi-threaded, non-blocking epoll I/O, lock-free, copy-free, SO_REUSEPORT. Handlers are pure (request)->[]u8 returning raw response bytes. JSON is built in a single allocation with precomputed prefixes (no per-request reflection); json-comp gzips on Accept-Encoding; json-tls terminates TLS 1.3 (Mbed TLS 4) on :8081 with ALPN http/1.1, reusing the same allocation-free /json serializer; static assets are preloaded into memory; fortunes renders the DB rows + a runtime row with HTML escaping; async-db uses the stdlib db.pg ConnectionPool. Pinned V 0.5.1 (prebuilt release). crud uses an in-memory cache-aside (X-Cache MISS/HIT, invalidated on update) — no Redis required.

vanilla-h2c.description: HTTP/2 cleartext (h2c, prior-knowledge) on vanilla's conn-mode seam: one epoll engine drives the RFC 9113 state machine behind a ConnHandler. The client's PRI * HTTP/2.0 preface parses as an ordinary request; the HTTP handler flips the connection over (core.queue_takeover), appends the server SETTINGS preface, and every later burst is fed to the http2 machine instead of the HTTP/1.1 parser. The http2 module is a self-contained RFC 9113/7541 codec: HPACK (static + dynamic table, canonical Huffman decode, decoded-block ceiling), frame codec, and a stream state machine with send-side flow control, hardened against a live h2spec CI gate. Requests surface only when COMPLETE (END_STREAM); responses are HPACK-encoded HEADERS + DATA. The :8082 listener is h2c-only — a plain HTTP/1.1 request is refused 505, never a 200, so the benchmark cannot silently measure h1 throughput. /json reuses the vanilla /json shape (same dataset, precomputed per-item prefixes, total = price*quantity*m). Multi-threaded, SO_REUSEPORT, lock-free, -gc none. Pinned V 0.5.2 (prebuilt from source).

vanilla-io_uring.description: vanilla is a minimalist, high-performance HTTP server written in V: multi-threaded, non-blocking io_uring I/O, lock-free, copy-free, SO_REUSEPORT. This entry is the vanilla-epoll entry's async handler verbatim, running on the io_uring async runtime (enghitalo/vanilla#99): DB queries park on the PG socket via a oneshot IORING_OP_POLL_ADD and resume on the ring — never blocking the worker. JSON is built in a single allocation with precomputed prefixes (no per-request reflection); json-comp gzips on Accept-Encoding; json-tls serves /json over HTTP/1.1 + TLS 1.3 on :8081 via the lib's epoll backend (the io_uring backend has no TLS) with kTLS record offload where present; static assets are preloaded into memory; fortunes renders the DB rows + a runtime row with HTML escaping; async-db/crud/fortunes use the native async pg_async driver with per-worker pipelined pools. Built with the default GC on pinned V master (built from source). crud uses an in-memory cache-aside (X-Cache MISS/HIT, invalidated on update) — no Redis required.

vanilla-ws.description: WebSocket echo on vanilla's conn-mode seam: one epoll engine, two protocols on the same connection. The HTTP handler validates the RFC 6455 upgrade as a pure function, appends the 101 and hands the connection over (core.queue_takeover); from then on every readable burst is fed to a ConnHandler instead of the HTTP/1.1 state machine. The websocket module is a pure RFC 6455 codec (accept-key, frame-head parsing, in-place unmasking, unmasked server-frame writers). Read buffering/compaction, batched flushes and EPOLLOUT backpressure are the engine's own, so a pipelined burst of frames is drained in one handler call and coalesced into one write. Multi-threaded, SO_REUSEPORT, lock-free, -gc none.

varnish.description: Varnish Cache HTTP accelerator with native TLS/H2 termination (-A). A custom vmod (Rust, varnish-rs) computes /baseline11 and /baseline2 in-process; vmod-fileserver serves /static.

veb.description: veb is the web framework in V's standard library, now running on the parallel fasthttp backend (multi-threaded, SO_REUSEPORT epoll, zero-copy append handler). Its deterministic request framing reassembles TCP-fragmented requests and decodes chunked bodies, so baseline is subscribed (the old single-threaded backend could not). JSON responses are built without per-request reflection (precomputed item prefixes + manual serialization); json-comp gzips on Accept-Encoding with a process-shared cache; static assets are served via veb's static handler (sendfile + MIME) mounted at /static/; crud is an in-memory cache-aside (X-Cache MISS/HIT, invalidated on update); fortunes renders the DB rows + a runtime row with HTML escaping; async-db/crud/fortunes use the stdlib db.pg pooled Go-style DB. Built on pinned V master 84a76d791 (the fasthttp vanilla-architecture refactor, vlang/v#27771) with the default GC (Boehm). json-tls is not subscribed: it needs a second TLS listener on :8081 (a separate OpenSSL path) not wired here.

vertx.description: Eclipse Vert.x 5 with vertx-web on Netty, one server verticle per core. Routing and query/path params through the Router API, JsonObject serialization, gzip through the server compression option.

vibe.d.description: vibe.d 0.10 on its own fiber based event loop, default configuration, one listener task per core sharing the port with SO_REUSEPORT. Routing through URLRouter, JSON through vibe.data.json, gzip through the built-in Accept-Encoding negotiation. json-tls on 8081 through vibe-stream:tls on OpenSSL, one listener per worker like the plaintext port.

warp.description: Warp 3.3 serving a plain WAI Application on the threaded GHC runtime, default configuration, one capability per core. Routing on the WAI request path, JSON through the aeson encoding API, gzip through the wai-extra Gzip middleware.

zeemo.description: Bare-metal Zig HTTP/1.1 server on io_uring. One reactor process per logical CPU via SO_REUSEPORT, hand-written incremental parser, registered provided-buffer rings.

zio-http.description: ZIO HTTP 3.11 on the Netty backend with ZIO 2, default configuration. Routing through the Routes DSL, JSON through zio-json, gzip through the server's own response compression.

zix.description: HTTP/1.1 on the zix.Http1 raw engine, .URING dispatch: per-worker SO_REUSEPORT io_uring loops, comptime Router, staged send sink. Dual listener: cleartext 8080, TLS 1.3 on 8081. Database routes run on engine-worker lanes, each worker pumping its own pipelined postgrez connections on its ring with named prepared statements. No response cache and no startup pre-serialization anywhere: json serializes every field per request and compresses per request, static opens the file per request. The crud row cache is the 200 ms cache-aside the crud profile itself defines.

variants.description: Zig gRPC server on the zix.Grpc engine (native h2 framing), .URING dispatch: shared-nothing per-core io_uring with SO_REUSEPORT, unary plus server-streaming with DATA-frame coalescing. Dual listener (config.tls_port): h2c 8080 plus gRPC over TLS 1.3 on 8443, one process.

Zig HTTP/2 server on the zix.Http2 raw engine, .URING dispatch: shared-nothing per-core io_uring with SO_REUSEPORT, per-worker stream-slot pool. Dual listener (config.tls_port): h2c 8082 plus h2 over TLS 1.3 (ALPN h2) on 8443, one process.

Zig HTTP/3 server on the zix.Http3 engine, pure-Zig QUIC on std.crypto (RFC 9000/9001/9002/9114), .URING dispatch: one SO_REUSEPORT worker per core on UDP 8443, NewReno with PTO retransmit, rolling MAX_STREAMS/MAX_DATA credit. A one-worker https responder on TCP 8443 answers the readiness probe, idle during the run.

WebSocket echo on the zix.Http1 engine, .URING dispatch. GET /ws upgrades and the engine drives the frame pump: frames are echoed on readiness and a pipelined burst leaves as one write. No cache anywhere, echo is per connection.
